q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q29) Which one of the following is different: 62, 31, 34, 17, 20?
facts: Each of 62 and 31, and of 34 and 17, forms a pair where one is double the other. 20 has no partner (10 is missing), so it is different.
rel: Tip: look for pairs related by doubling or halving; the leftover number is the odd one.
note: Sequence 62,31,34,17,20 follows /2, +3 alternating, so no true odd one out; rewrite as "What comes next: 62, 31, 34, 17, 20, ?" answer 10 (include 10 in options)

q: Which one is different from the rest: X5, Y6, Z9?
facts: The numbers follow the letters in order: X is followed by 5 and Y by 6, so Z should be followed by 7. Z9 breaks the pattern.
rel: X, Y and Z are the 24th, 25th and 26th letters of the alphabet.
note: No clear rule makes any of X5, Y6, Z9 different; the explanation (X5, Y6, so Z should be 7) is an invented rule and "All are the same" is also arguable. Replace with a clear pattern question, e.g. "Odd one out: 3, 5, 9, 11" with an unambiguous rule. Pure logic, no search needed.
